zh.question: 一片叶子从芽到落下，做过哪些工作，为什么会变色？
zh.observe: 先在同一根枝条上回看幼叶展开，再停在成熟阶段追踪根到叶的水。进入同一叶面位置的组织、细胞和色素区室；比较黄、红两路，最后观察离层与脱落。叶龄、水的旅程和观察尺度分开控制。

academic.title: 幼叶展开，成熟叶连接植物与空气
academic.body: 本例从芽中的叶开始，不从种子开始。幼叶生长展开后，叶脉中的木质部为叶肉供应水；叶内蒸发、水分子内聚和水势梯度参与维持从根到叶的运输，水汽经气孔扩散出去。气孔调节气体交换与失水，并非始终固定开度。光合作用利用光能，糖的碳来自二氧化碳；植物活细胞白天和夜晚也呼吸。根到叶的水运路线图是结构示意，不是枝条的等比例地图。

academic.title: 衰老中的资源回收与色素变化
academic.body: 日长、温度和植物自身状态影响叶片衰老；部分光合作用装置被拆解，氮、磷等资源可回运到其他部位。叶绿素减少使原有类胡萝卜素更显眼；一些植物新合成的花青素积累在液泡，而不是叶绿体变红。黄、红是两种能力的对照，不是所有叶子的固定先后顺序；多种色素可以共存，具体颜色和时序受物种与环境影响。

academic.title: 离层、脱落与首版边界
academic.body: 在叶柄基部，离层相关变化使叶与枝条的连接减弱，脱落后枝条留下痕迹。叶片不再由这条连接接收根部水流。首版以连续形变表示展开与脱落，以定性状态表示衰老与色素，不计算细胞分裂、真实风力轨迹、细胞死亡后的崩解或落叶分解。常绿植物也更换叶子，但不同叶龄的叶可同时存在，不能把每片叶都塞进同一年四季时间表。

zh.misconception: 红叶不是所有叶子的终点；黄色不一定变红，叶绿素也不是变成另一种色素。植物不只在夜里呼吸，常绿也不表示一片叶永远不落。
zh.boundary: 同一叶片身份贯穿展开、衰老与脱落，回退只重访教学状态。各图有不同放大比例；形变、色素趋势、运输标记和时序均为定性示意，不能当作特定物种预测。显微图覆盖展开后至脱落前的代表组织，不展示幼芽内部发育或死亡后崩解。首版未模拟落叶分解与生态循环。

narration.label: 从芽中开始
narration.text: 先记住这根枝条。芽里有一片小小的叶，它慢慢展开，叶缘变大，却一直连在原来的位置。我们跟着的是同一片叶，不是在翻看四张不同的图片。等它展开，再靠近看看它每天做什么。
narration.cue: 从幼叶停靠点拖到成熟，观察固定枝条和同一叶缘。

narration.label: 成熟叶的工作
narration.text: 成熟的叶子与整株植物相连。水从根进入，沿着木质部来到叶脉。一部分水在叶内蒸发，水汽经过气孔进入空气。实心标记变成空心，是在提醒我们相态变了，不是水滴从气孔喷出来。有光时，叶肉细胞还能利用光能制造糖；活细胞白天和夜晚也都会呼吸。
narration.cue: 成熟阶段打开水运；暂停在叶内，对照主叶片、根到叶路线和气孔窗口。

narration.label: 衰老与不同的颜色
narration.text: 慢慢走向衰老阶段。树从叶子里收回一些营养，绿色的叶绿素减少，原有的黄色更容易看见。有些叶子还会制造花青素，在液泡里积累，于是显出红色。红色和黄色是两条不同的路径，不是每片叶子都先黄再红。走进同一处叶片，看看不同色素住在哪里。
narration.cue: 黄红对照，进入组织、细胞，再分别观察叶绿体与液泡。

narration.label: 离开枝条，不是重新出生
narration.text: 叶柄与枝条之间的连接逐渐减弱，叶片离开了。看，枝条上的痕迹还在，原来那片叶也还在画面里。它不再从根得到这条水流。真实落叶以后还会干燥、碎裂，被分解者利用，这里先停在脱落这一站。下一年长出来的是新的叶子，不是这片旧叶变回了小芽。
narration.cue: 到脱落终点，核对枝条痕迹与运输停止；说明回退仅为重看。

en.question: What does a leaf do from its bud to detachment, and why does its colour change?
en.observe: Follow a young leaf unfolding on the same branch, pause at maturity and track water from roots. Enter the same leaf patch, cells and pigment compartments. Compare yellow and red routes, then inspect abscission and detachment. Leaf age, water progress and observation scale are separate.

academic.title: An expanding leaf connects the plant and air
academic.body: This example starts with a leaf in a bud, not a seed. As it expands, xylem in its veins supplies mesophyll with water. Evaporation within leaves, water cohesion and water-potential gradients help maintain root-to-leaf transport; vapour diffuses through stomata. Stomata regulate exchange and water loss rather than remaining at a fixed opening. Light powers photosynthesis, while sugar carbon comes from carbon dioxide. Living plant cells also respire in day and night. The root-to-leaf diagram is structural, not a scale map of the branch.

academic.title: Resource recovery and pigment changes during senescence
academic.body: Day length, temperature and plant condition influence senescence. Some photosynthetic machinery is dismantled and nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus can be remobilised. Chlorophyll loss reveals existing carotenoids; anthocyanins made by some plants accumulate in vacuoles, not reddening chloroplasts. Yellow and red compare capabilities rather than a universal sequence. Pigments coexist, and species and environment influence timing and appearance.

academic.title: Abscission, detachment and first-version limits
academic.body: Changes near the stalk base weaken the connection; detachment leaves a scar on the branch. The leaf no longer receives root-supplied water through that connection. Continuous deformation illustrates expansion and detachment, with qualitative senescence and pigment states. Cell division, real wind-driven trajectories, cellular collapse after death and litter decomposition are not calculated. Evergreen plants replace leaves too, but multiple leaf ages may coexist rather than following one shared annual schedule.

en.misconception: Not every leaf ends red: yellow need not turn red and chlorophyll does not become another pigment. Plants do not respire only at night, and evergreen does not mean an individual leaf lasts forever.
en.boundary: The same leaf persists through expansion, senescence and detachment; backward scrubbing revisits teaching states. Views have different magnifications. Shape changes, pigment trends, water markers and timing are qualitative, not species predictions. Microscopy represents expanded tissue before detachment, not bud development or postmortem collapse. Litter decomposition and ecosystem cycling are not simulated.

narration.label: Starting in a bud
narration.text: Remember this branch. A small leaf unfolds from its bud. Its edge expands while its stalk stays at the same place. We are following one leaf, not turning four unrelated pictures. When it has expanded, move closer to discover its work.
narration.cue: Move from the bud stop to maturity and follow the fixed branch and leaf edge.

narration.label: A mature leaf at work
narration.text: The leaf is connected to the whole plant. Water enters the roots and travels through xylem to the veins. Some evaporates inside the leaf and diffuses through stomata. A filled marker becoming hollow indicates a change of phase, not drops spraying from a pore. In light, mesophyll cells also use light energy to make sugars. Living cells respire during both day and night.
narration.cue: Open water transport at maturity and pause inside the leaf; compare the main leaf, transport diagram and pore window.

narration.label: Senescence and different colours
narration.text: Move towards senescence. The tree recovers some nutrients, green chlorophyll decreases and existing yellow becomes easier to see. Some leaves also make anthocyanins that accumulate in vacuoles and give red colours. These are different routes; not every leaf goes from yellow to red. Enter the same patch and locate its pigments.
narration.cue: Compare yellow and red, then tissue, cell, chloroplast and vacuole.

narration.label: Leaving the branch is not rebirth
narration.text: The connection between stalk and branch weakens and the leaf detaches. Its scar remains, and the same leaf is still visible. It no longer receives that root-supplied water flow. Real litter later dries, fragments and is used by decomposers; this model stops at detachment. Next year's leaf is new, not this old leaf turning back into a bud.
narration.cue: Inspect detachment, the persistent scar and stopped water transport. Explain that scrubbing backward only revisits a state.
